title: Which prompt is better?
question: You need to prepare a short talk for your classmates about why sleep matters. Which prompt will give the most useful answer?

options.why: There's no task, audience or format, so the answer will be generic.

options.text: Write everything you know about sleep in great detail.
options.why: You'll get a long text that doesn't fit a short talk.

options.text: Give 5 points for a 2-minute talk for 8th graders: why sleep matters for memory. Simple words and one real-life example.
options.why: It has a task, an audience, a format and a length.

hint: Look for the option that states the audience and the format.

title: What can you send to a chatbot?
question: You want AI to help you write an application letter. Which option is safer?

options.text: Paste a template with your ID number, address and phone number.
options.why: It's better not to send ID numbers, addresses or phone numbers: the AI doesn't need them to help with wording.

options.text: Ask for a template with placeholders like [Full name], [address], [date] and fill it in yourself.
options.why: The AI helps with the text, and your personal data stays with you.

options.text: Send a photo of your passport so the AI fills everything in.
options.why: This is the riskiest option: the document contains a lot of personal data.

hint: Think about what data the AI actually needs to help with the text.

title: Improve the prompt
question: Rewrite the prompt “Write about ecology” so the answer can be used straight away.
checklist: There's a task: what exactly to do
It says who it's for or why
A format or length is set
There's a constraint: tone, difficulty or what to leave out
hint: Use the four parts of a prompt: task, context, format, constraints.
sample: Prepare 6 tips on how school students can throw away less plastic. It's for a 5th-grade wall newspaper: each tip no longer than one sentence, simple words, no scare tactics.

title: A suspicious quote
question: The AI gave you a quote from a famous scientist with a link to an article. The link doesn't open. What should you do?

options.text: Use the quote: the AI gave a link, so it's real.
options.why: AI can invent quotes and links that look real.

options.text: Search for the quote in reliable sources. If you can't find it, don't use it.
options.why: Use a quote only if a source confirms it.

options.text: Reword it slightly and use it without a link.
options.why: That presents an unconfirmed fact as true, which is dishonest.

hint: Who should confirm the quote: the AI or a source?

title: A tutor prompt
question: Write a prompt in which the AI explains a topic and then quizzes you, without giving answers in advance.
checklist: Your level is stated (grade, course, what you already know)
It asks for questions one at a time
It asks not to give answers in advance
hint: Start with what you already know and what's unclear.
sample: I'm in 10th grade and understand what a function is, but I get confused by derivatives. Explain derivatives using a car's speed as an example, then ask me 4 questions one at a time. Don't show answers until I reply.

title: Describing a picture
question: You described an image as “a cat in a room”, but the result is too random. What should you add first?

options.text: Words like “very beautiful, best quality, masterpiece”.
options.why: General praise barely specifies what to draw.

options.text: Style, angle, light and details: “a ginger cat on a windowsill, side view, evening light, watercolour”.
options.why: Specific details make the result predictable.

options.text: Repeat the same prompt until it works.
options.why: Repeating without changes gives another random result.

hint: Remember the five elements of a description.

title: Break a goal into steps
question: Write a prompt that helps break your big goal into steps that fit your free time.
checklist: It says when you have free time
The step size or plan format is set
hint: The AI doesn't know your schedule until you tell it.
sample: My goal is to read a 300-page book in 3 weeks. On weekdays I have 30 minutes in the evening, at weekends an hour. Make a day-by-day plan as a table and keep one rest day a week.

title: A key in the code
question: Your code doesn't work and you want to show it to the AI. It contains a line with your secret API key. What do you do?

options.text: Send it as is, it's easier to debug.
options.why: Your secret key could end up with strangers, and you don't control where it's stored.

options.text: Replace the key with “YOUR_API_KEY” and then send it.
options.why: The AI can understand the code without the real key.

options.text: Delete all the code and describe the problem in one word.
options.why: Without the code and the error message, the AI can't help.

hint: Does the AI need the real key to find the bug?

title: Study rules
question: Your teacher said the essay must be written without AI. What's the honest thing to do?

options.text: Generate the essay and rewrite it a bit so nobody notices.
options.why: That breaks the rules and passes off someone else's work as yours.

options.text: Write the essay yourself. If the rules allow it, use AI for preparation, for example to understand the topic.
options.why: You follow the rules and still learn.

options.text: Ask a friend to generate the essay for you.
options.why: The rule is broken just the same, with someone else involved.

hint: If you're not sure what's allowed, ask your teacher.
